name: IL-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Mike Quigley running with large cash advantage
Republican challenger underfunded with no visible campaign infrastructure
Prediction markets price near-certain Democratic win
model.rationale: Quigley holds a heavily Democratic Chicago-area seat with a D+19 lean, a $1.2 million war chest, and no serious opposition spending against him, while Polymarket prices his win at 95%. Fundamentals point to a margin in the mid-20s, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A surprise strong Republican fundraising push or an unexpected Quigley scandal would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Quigley, a well-established Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a Chicago-area district that leans Democratic by about 19 points. He has raised over $725,000 and holds nearly $1.2 million on hand, while Republican Tommy Hanson reports no meaningful fundraising or outside support. No outside groups are spending against Quigley, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Quigley roughly a 95% chance of winning, and the fundamentals point to a victory margin in the mid-20s. With no public polling and no signs of a competitive Republican campaign, this race sits firmly in the Safe Democratic category, with high confidence in the outcome.
